current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 135th G.A. (2023-2024) and 136th G.A. (2025-2026) via the codes.ohio.gov version history for R.C. 149.43. Fee-relevant changes in the 2024-2026 window: (1) H.B. 315, 135th G.A., eff. April 9, 2025, added the law-enforcement/prosecutor video-record cost paragraph to (B)(1) — actual cost incl. staff time/overhead, capped at $75 per hour of video produced and $750 total, optional prepayment of the estimate with the production duty starting on full payment, estimate within five business days, overrun capped at 20% with advance notice; (2) H.B. 96, 136th G.A. (budget), eff. Sept. 30, 2025, added (B)(11) — no fee for victims/counsel/insurers on affidavit; (3) H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026 (enacted-awaiting-effect), amends definitions in (A) only — the fee/payment language ((B)(1), (B)(6), (B)(7), (B)(11), (E)(2), (F)) is verbatim-identical in the Sept. 7, 2026 version (diffed). Codified statutes were available and opened (current version eff. Sept. 30, 2025 and the Sept. 7, 2026 version). Ohio delegates NO fee figure to any administrative rule or uniform schedule: 'at cost' (= actual cost, Warren Newspapers v. Hutson 1994) is the only standard for all public offices, and the AG's model policy leaves the per-page and per-disc figures as fill-in values for each office. Guidance-vs-law: the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual and undated Model Public Records Policy were opened; they restate statute and case law and add no municipal figure; the manual's statements on nonpayment (Fragale/Dehler), the notice-of-amount-due duty (Ware v. Akron 2021) and no-certified-copies duty (Mobley v. LaRose 2024) are recorded as Official Guidance because the underlying opinions were not opened.

Applies to every 'public office' (state, county, city, village, township, school district — R.C. 149.43(A)(1)); Ohio runs one regime for all public bodies and has no separate state-agency fee schedule.

resolutions.source_language: Ohio does not specify any charge for search and/or review time in R.C. 149.43. ... Since respondents are already compensated for performing their duties, and responding to public records requests is merely another duty, the cost set forth in R.C. 149.43(B) should not include labor costs regarding employee time. Respondents' policy to the contrary was inconsistent with that provision. Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs.

new_rules.legal_concept: 'At cost' means 'actual cost'; the office sets its copy fee by policy reflecting actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: The 'at cost' standard of R.C. 149.43(B) means 'actual cost'; a public office, in its sound discretion, may adopt a reasonable policy setting a fee for copies that reflects the actual costs involved in making a copy, unless the cost is otherwise set by statute.
new_rules.trigger: A public office charges for copies of public records.
new_rules.source_language: Although the court has not defined "at cost," it has been stated that a public office, in its sound discretion, may adopt a reasonable policy setting a fee for copies obtained from the public office, with the fee reflecting the actual costs involved in making a copy, unless the cost is otherwise set by statute. 1989 Ohio Atty.Gen.Ops. No. 89-073; cf. State ex rel. Nelson v. Fuerst (1993), 66 Ohio St.3d 47, 48, 607 N.E.2d 836, 838, where the court referred in dicta to "reasonable cost" in a public records case. Since the General Assembly could have, but failed to, specify "reasonable cost," we hold that R.C. 149.43(B) means "actual cost."
new_rules.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 25 (Ohio 1994)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio, decided Oct. 26, 1994; still cited as controlling in the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual, ch. 2 § 12 n.174)
new_rules.notes: Municipal case (Warren police department). Confirms that the operative per-page value is set by the city's own policy under an actual-cost ceiling; Ohio has no statewide per-page rate. Cites 1989 OAG 89-073 (policy may set fee reflecting actual costs). Secondary type: Permission (city may adopt a fee policy).

new_rules.legal_concept: Employee labor / staff time not chargeable under 'at cost'
new_rules.atomic_rule: The cost chargeable for copies under R.C. 149.43(B) shall not include labor costs regarding employee time (search, review, or copying time); Ohio specifies no charge for search and/or review time.
new_rules.trigger: A public office computes the charge for copies of public records (any record type other than law-enforcement/prosecutor video records under R.C. 149.43(B)(1) para. 2).
new_rules.source_language: Ohio does not specify any charge for search and/or review time in R.C. 149.43. ... Since respondents are already compensated for performing their duties, and responding to public records requests is merely another duty, the cost set forth in R.C. 149.43(B) should not include labor costs regarding employee time. Respondents' policy to the contrary was inconsistent with that provision. Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs.
new_rules.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 26 (Ohio 1994); syllabus: 'Copies of public records available at actual cost without charges for labor or employee time.'
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio 1994; restated in AG 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual ch. 2 § 12: 'Except in rare exceptions, the cost of employee time cannot be included in the cost of copies or of delivery.')
new_rules.notes: Ellipsis in source_language omits only the FOIA comparison and Florida quotation between the two operative sentences; the quoted sentences are verbatim. Statutory exception: video records of state/local law enforcement or prosecutors (OH-9011), where 'actual cost' expressly includes staff time and overhead, capped at $75/hour of video produced and $750 total (OH-0019). A reasonable private-contractor copying/extraction cost may be passed through (Gibbs v. Concord Twp. 2003-Ohio-1586; Gambill v. Opperman 2013-Ohio-761, per Manual n.177) — not opened this pass.

new_rules.legal_concept: Flat/minimum charge not tied to actual copying cost impermissible
new_rules.atomic_rule: A charge for copies that is not tied to the actual copying costs (e.g., a $5 charge for the initial page of each file) is inconsistent with the 'at cost' requirement.
new_rules.trigger: A public office's fee policy imposes a flat, minimum, or initial-page charge for copies.
new_rules.source_language: Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs. See, e.g., State ex rel. Bonnell v. Cleveland (Aug. 26, 1993), Cuyahoga App. No. 64854, unreported, 1993 WL 335426 (court relied on stipulated evidence regarding actual per-page copying costs consisting of costs of toner, paper and copying time). Relator's third proposition is sustained.
new_rules.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 26 (Ohio 1994)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio 1994; AG 2026 Manual n.174 summarizes: 'public office cannot charge $5 for initial page or for employee labor, but only for "actual cost" of final copies')
new_rules.notes: The court's finding was evidentiary (no evidence tying the $5 to cost) rather than a per-se rule; treat as: any minimum/flat charge must be supported by actual copying cost. Bonnell (cited) describes actual per-page cost components as toner, paper and copying time.

new_rules.legal_concept: Customized/compiled documents: no charge for employee labor or computer programming time
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a public office creates a customized document by coordinating and compiling information from its public records, the fee under R.C. 149.43(B) is limited to actual costs, exclusive of any charges for employee labor or computer programming time in preparation or production.
new_rules.trigger: A requester asks for a customized/compiled document (data extraction, custom report or map) generated from existing public records.
new_rules.source_language: For purposes of determining the fee that may be charged pursuant to R.C. 149.43(B) for a customized document created by coordinating and compiling information from public records, "at cost" means actual costs, exclusive of any charges for employee labor or computer programming time involved in either the preparation or actual production of the document.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (listed in the AG's 'Opinions Interpreting Ohio's Sunshine Laws' index; not overruled)
new_rules.notes: Opinion was addressed to a county prosecutor (county offices) but reasons from R.C. 149.43(B) and Hutson, which bind all public offices including municipalities; applicability to a city is by parity of reasoning (flag). Contrast R.C. 149.43(F) (Bureau of Motor Vehicles only): 'special extraction costs' incl. programming time plus 10% — state-agency-only, not a municipal rule.

new_rules.legal_concept: Digital-delivery cap of ten records per month for offices with a free, fully searchable public website
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public office that provides some or all of its public records on a website that is fully accessible and searchable at all times (other than acts of God or maintenance) and charges no fee to search, access, download, or receive records there may limit to ten per month the number of records it will deliver in a digital format to a person, unless the records are not provided on the website and unless the person certifies in writing non-commercial use.

new_rules.source_language: A public office that chooses to provide some or all of its public records on a web site that is fully accessible to and searchable by members of the public at all times, other than during acts of God outside the public office's control or maintenance, and that charges no fee to search, access, download, or otherwise receive records provided on the web site, may limit to ten per month the number of records requested by a person that the office will deliver in a digital format, unless the requested records are not provided on the web site and unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.

new_rules.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: prepayment of estimated actual cost may be required; production obligation begins on full payment
new_rules.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office may include in its public records policy a requirement that the requester pay the estimated actual cost before it begins preparing a video record; where it does, its obligation to produce the video or make it available for inspection begins once the estimated actual cost is paid in full.

new_rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'reasonable period of time' (copies) / 'promptly' (inspection) runs from full payment of the estimated actual cost
new_rules.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may include in its public records policy the requirement that a requester pay the estimated actual cost before beginning the process of preparing a video record for inspection or production. Where a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office imposes such a requirement, its obligation to produce a video or make it available for inspection begins once the estimated actual cost is paid in full by the requester.

new_rules.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall provide the requester with the estimated actual cost of preparing a video record within five business days of receipt of the public records request.
new_rules.trigger: Receipt of a public records request for a video record by a state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
new_rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of the public records request (estimated actual cost to requester)
new_rules.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall provide the requester with the estimated actual cost within five business days of receipt of the public records request.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
new_rules.notes: Statute text is unconditional ('shall provide'); the AG Manual reads it as applying where prepayment is required ('If prepayment is required, the agency must provide a cost estimate within five business days'). Record-specific; no general estimate deadline exists for other records.

new_rules.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: overrun collectible only with advance notice and capped at 20% of estimate
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the actual cost of a video record exceeds the estimated actual cost, the agency may charge the difference upon fulfilling the request only if the requester was notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimate, and shall not charge a difference exceeding twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
new_rules.trigger: Actual cost of preparing a video record exceeds the estimate given to the requester.
new_rules.source_language: If the actual cost exceeds the estimated actual cost, a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester for the difference upon fulfilling a request for video records if the requester is notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimated actual cost. A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a requester a difference that exceeds twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
new_rules.notes: ceiling: 20% of the estimated actual cost (overrun); plus a required advance notice (secondary type: Requirement). Combined with the $750 total cap (OH-0019). No revised-estimate mechanism; no such rule for non-video records.

new_rules.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: 'actual cost' includes staff time and overhead
new_rules.atomic_rule: For video records only, 'actual cost' means all costs incurred by the state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office in reviewing, blurring or otherwise obscuring, redacting, uploading, or producing the video, including the storage medium, staff time, and any other relevant overhead necessary to comply with the request.
new_rules.trigger: Charge computed for preparing a video record for inspection or production by a state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
new_rules.source_language: As used in this division, "actual cost," with respect to video records only, means all costs incurred by the state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office in reviewing, blurring or otherwise obscuring, redacting, uploading, or producing the video records, including but not limited to the storage medium on which the record is produced, staff time, and any other relevant overhead necessary to comply with the request.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
new_rules.notes: The one statutory exception to Ohio's no-labor rule (OH-9002). Bounded by OH-0019 ($75 per hour of VIDEO PRODUCED — not per staff hour — and $750 total). AG Manual ch. 2 § 13: charges must reflect documentable actual costs; a flat uniform per-hour rate 'may fail to reflect the actual costs and could be challenged'.

new_rules.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: no fee for victims (or their counsel/insurer) on affidavit
new_rules.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a fee for preparing or copying a video record when the requester is a victim (Ohio Const. art. I § 10a, or a tort victim under R.C. 2307.011) who reasonably asserts the video relates to the act or omission that caused the harm, or the victim's legal counsel or insurer; the fee may only be waived upon receipt of an affidavit by the victim or counsel identifying that the video will be used to investigate harm or damages captured on it.
new_rules.trigger: Video-record request by a qualifying victim, victim's legal counsel (with retention agreement/letter of representation), or victim's insurer, accompanied by the required affidavit.
new_rules.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a fee for preparing a video record for inspection, or producing a copy of a video record, when the requester of the video record is a victim, as defined in Ohio Constitution, Article I, Section 10a, or who is a victim who suffered loss and could seek remedy through a tort action as defined by section 2307.011 of the Revised Code, who reasonably asserts that the video recording relates to the act or omission that caused the victim's harm or loss, or who is the legal counsel or insurer of the victim. A fee under this section may only be waived upon the receipt of an affidavit by the victim or the victim's legal counsel identifying that the use of the video is to investigate harm or damages that may have been captured on the video.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (division (B)(11) added eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) version)
new_rules.notes: Mandatory waiver (Prohibition on charging) gated on an affidavit — the only fee-waiver rule in Ohio's Public Records Act. 'Legal counsel of the victim' is defined in the same division (attorney producing a signed retention agreement or letter of representation). No general fee-waiver grounds exist for other records; discretionary waivers are a matter of local policy.

new_rules.legal_concept: No duty to furnish copies without payment
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public office has no obligation to provide free copies to a requester who cannot or will not pay the cost of copies.
new_rules.trigger: Requester declines or fails to pay the (advance) cost of copies.
new_rules.source_language: There is no obligation to provide free copies to someone who cannot or will not pay.
new_rules.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22), citing State ex rel. Call v. Fragale, 2004-Ohio-6589, ¶ 6; State ex rel. Dehler v. Mohr, 2011-Ohio-959, ¶ 3
new_rules.effective_status: Current (2026 edition of the AG manual, opened; underlying decisions not opened this pass)
new_rules.notes: Guidance restating case law; the underlying opinions (Fragale; Dehler) were not opened — flag manual verification of the holdings. No statutory withdrawal period (N days) exists; the request simply is not fulfilled until payment.

new_rules.legal_concept: Notice of amount due must precede any denial for nonpayment
new_rules.atomic_rule: Before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due.
new_rules.trigger: Office intends to withhold copies because the requester has not paid.
new_rules.source_language: However, before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due.
new_rules.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22), citing State ex rel. Ware v. City of Akron, 2021-Ohio-624, ¶ 13-15
new_rules.effective_status: Current (2026 edition of the AG manual, opened; Ware v. Akron not opened this pass)
new_rules.notes: A required cost notice with no dollar threshold — the notice is due whenever payment is a precondition. Ware v. Akron (municipal) per the manual: office complied when it identified the cost of copies and offered copies upon payment. Flag: verify holding text in the opinion.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG Model Public Records Policy: per-page and per-disc charges are fill-in values under 'actual cost, not labor'
new_rules.atomic_rule: The AG's model policy (which public offices may use under R.C. 149.43(E)(2)) provides that requesters may be charged only the actual cost of making copies, not labor, with the office's paper per-page charge and per-disc charge entered as its own values.
new_rules.trigger: A public office adopts its public records policy and sets its copy charges.
new_rules.source_language: Those seeking public records may be charged only the actual cost of making copies, not labor. The charge for paper copies is [X] cents per page. The charge for electronic files downloaded to a compact disc is [X] per disc.
new_rules.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, Model Public Records Request Policy (developed under R.C. 109.43(E)), 'Copying and Mailing Costs'
new_rules.effective_status: Current (undated model; posted on the AG site; opened 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Confirms defers-to-city under an actual-cost ceiling: '[X] cents per page' and '[X] per disc' are placeholders the office fills in. Guidance, not law; the AG model is optional ('may obtain guidance from the model'). Model is undated — flag manual verification of currency.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG Model Policy: delivery at actual cost; no charge for e-mailed documents
new_rules.atomic_rule: Per the AG model policy, a requester who asks for delivery may be charged the actual cost of postage and mailing supplies or other actual costs of delivery, and there is no charge for e-mailed documents.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for delivery of copies (mail, other carrier, or e-mail).
new_rules.source_language: If a requester asks that documents be delivered to them, he or she may be charged the actual cost of the postage and mailing supplies, or other actual costs of delivery. There is no charge for e-mailed documents.
new_rules.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, Model Public Records Request Policy, 'Copying and Mailing Costs'
new_rules.notes: The 'no charge for e-mailed documents' line is guidance consistent with 'at cost' (no incremental cost); the statute (B)(7)(a) itself only authorizes actual delivery/supply costs.

new_rules.legal_concept: Motor-vehicle accident report copy: nonrefundable $4 fee (or county-approved amount); photos/electronic formats extra
new_rules.atomic_rule: The law enforcement agency that submitted an accident report shall furnish a copy of the report and associated documents to a person claiming an interest arising out of the accident (or the person's attorney) upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of four dollars, or the amount approved by the board of county commissioners under division (B); photographs or other electronic formats are charged in addition (above $4 only if county-approved).
new_rules.trigger: Request for a copy of a motor-vehicle accident report (submitted under R.C. 5502.11) by a person claiming an interest arising out of the accident or their attorney.
new_rules.source_language: The law enforcement agency that submitted a report shall furnish a copy of such report and associated documents to any person claiming an interest arising out of a motor vehicle accident, or to the person's attorney, upon the payment of a nonrefundable fee of four dollars or the amount approved by the board of county commissioners of the county in which the law enforcement agency is located as provided in division (B) of this section. The cost of photographs or any other electronic format shall be in addition to the nonrefundable four-dollar fee for the accident report, whether the report was submitted by the state highway patrol or another law enforcement agency. A law enforcement agency may charge a fee that is in excess of four dollars for photographs and other electronic formats if such a fee is approved by a board of county commissioners of the county in which the law enforcement agency is located as provided in division (B) of this section.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (eff. July 17, 2009, H.B. 1, 128th G.A.; no later amendment shown on codes.ohio.gov)
new_rules.notes: Binds every submitting 'law enforcement agency', including municipal police. Listed by the AG Manual as an exception to 'at cost' (Manual ch. 2 § 12; a specific fee statute controls over the general 'at cost' rule, R.C. 1.51). Scope limited to interested persons; whether a non-interested requester may obtain the report 'at cost' under 149.43 is not addressed — flag.

new_rules.legal_concept: Public records policy may not cap records per person or per period, nor impose a fixed response wait
new_rules.atomic_rule: Except as otherwise provided in R.C. 149.43 (e.g., the (B)(7) delivery caps), a public office's public records policy may not limit the number of public records it will make available to a single person, may not limit the number it will make available during a fixed period of time, and may not establish a fixed period of time before responding unless that period is less than eight hours.
new_rules.trigger: Public office adopts or applies its public records policy to a requester's volume or timing of requests.
new_rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the policy may not limit the number of public records that the public office will make available to a single person, may not limit the number of public records that it will make available during a fixed period of time, and may not establish a fixed period of time before it will respond to a request for inspection or copying of public records, unless that period is less than eight hours.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
new_rules.notes: Relevant to 'repeat/aggregated requests': Ohio permits no per-requester aggregation cap or fee aggregation; the only volume rule is the ten-per-month DELIVERY cap for commercial-purpose requesters. Concept key proposed (no existing key fits).

new_rules.atomic_rule: Public offices generally may not charge requesters for inspecting public records (including inspection of records posted online).
new_rules.trigger: Requester chooses to inspect rather than obtain copies.
new_rules.source_language: Generally, public offices may not charge requesters for inspecting public records.
new_rules.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws Manual, ch. 2 § 11 'Inspection at no cost during regular business hours' (p. 21), citing R.C. 149.43(B)(1) and 2014 Ohio Atty.Gen.Ops. No. 009
new_rules.notes: The statute states 'at cost' only for copies; the manual (and 2014 OAG 009, county auditor website) states the corollary that inspection carries no charge. Guidance restating statute/opinion.

applicability_notes: Ohio runs ONE regime: R.C. 149.43 applies to every 'public office' (state, county, city, village, township, school district). There is no state-agency uniform fee schedule and no administrative-code fee rule; every figure here binds municipalities except where noted.

Video-record cost paragraph, 5-business-day estimate, 20% overrun cap and (B)(11) victim exception are RECORD-SPECIFIC to 'a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office' — municipal police departments are covered; the city's non-law-enforcement records are not. Items av, estimate.revisionNotifyPercent, payment.reissue and waiver are resolved on that basis and flagged in their unit/notes.

R.C. 149.43(F) (bulk commercial special extraction: actual cost + special extraction costs + 10%) is Bureau of Motor Vehicles only — state_agencies_only; recorded as guidance in the commercial and overhead items, not applied to cities.

R.C. 5502.12 ($4 accident report) binds any submitting law enforcement agency, including municipal police, but only as to persons claiming an interest arising out of the accident (or their attorneys); a county board may approve a higher amount.

R.C. 313.10(B) (coroner $0.25/page, $1 minimum), R.C. 2303.20 (clerk of courts certified copies), R.C. 317.32 (county recorder) and R.C. 2301.21/2301.24 (court transcripts) are county/court fee statutes — noted as exceptions to 'at cost' per the AG manual, not municipal rules.

1999 OAG 99-012 was addressed to county offices; its no-labor/no-programming-time rule rests on R.C. 149.43(B) and Hutson, which bind municipalities — applied by parity of reasoning (flagged in the rule row).

The AG Model Public Records Policy is optional guidance ('may obtain guidance'); its '[X] cents per page' / '[X] per disc' placeholders confirm the per-page value is the city's to set under the actual-cost ceiling.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate (B&W, color, oversized) for municipalities — only 'at cost' = actual cost; the AG model policy leaves the figure blank for each office.

Labor (search, review/redaction, programming) is categorically NOT chargeable for municipal records (Hutson 1994; OAG 99-012); no hourly rate, overhead %, increment, or free-hours rule can exist. Sole exception: law-enforcement/prosecutor video records (staff time within actual cost, capped $75/hr of video produced, $750 total).

The prior slice's 'value_present' figures for dup.color.rate, dup.oversized.rate and dup.specialty.rate ($75, $750, 'five dollars') were misattributed: $75/$750 are the video caps and 'five dollars' is the initial-page charge struck down in Hutson.

No graduated page bands, free page allowance, de-minimis threshold, minimum fee, estimate threshold/validity/requester-response window, deposit threshold or deposit-percentage cap, nonpayment withdrawal period, fee forfeiture, commercial surcharge, certification fee, or fee-aggregation rule exists for municipalities in statute, AG rule/opinion, manual or model policy.
Ohio has no administrative-code public-records fee schedule; nothing was delegated to a rule for local governments (BMV rules under 149.43(F) are agency-only).
Existing rows OH-0023 and OH-0026 carried non-verbatim, partly incorrect source language (OH-0026's 'ninety-five per cent' condition is not in the statute) — amended by OH-9005 and OH-9006.

proposed_concept_keys.definition: A public records policy may not limit the number of records made available to a single person or during a fixed period, nor impose a fixed pre-response waiting period (Ohio R.C. 149.43(E)(2)); the structural counterpart to fee.aggregation — an express prohibition on per-requester aggregation caps.
